business.title: Team Dynamics Weaken When Employees Turn to AI instead of Colleagues
business.desc: Part of what makes a great team work is that people know and trust who has which skills or knowledge, and they know whom to go to for what. A new study shows how AI is changing this dynamic on teams: While AI use increased the sense that teammates had specialized and unique knowledge, treating AI as a teammate also eroded teammates’ trust in each other and their ability to coordinate. This practice of displacing teammates with AI can lead to “relationslipping”—the pernicious weakening of a team’s working relationships as its members substitute AI for each other. There are two ways this happens. First, when team members skip conversations in favor of a quick answer from AI, they aren’t developing or updating their mental map of who knows what. And second, when their colleagues offload their work to AI, those colleagues’ thinking becomes harder to see, so the map loses accuracy. That said, AI isn’t inherently bad for teams. Leaders can adopt a few practices to protect team cohesion, such as: increasing asynchronous communication, building psychological safety, rethinking teamwork with new norms and aligned incentives, and using AI to prepare for conversations instead of replacing them.

business.title: Predicting nitrogen dioxide column density from the International Wealth Index with a convolutional neural network in Africa
business.desc: In the pursuit of improving socioeconomic living conditions of their populations, many nations struggle to meet their nationally determined contributions (NDCs) under the Paris agreement, and that shortfall makes accountability for emissions reductions critical. The long atmospheric lifetimes of key gases such as carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4) hinder traditional greenhouse gas (GHG) monitoring, because what any one place emits adds only a small excess to a large, well-mixed background. Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) behaves differently: it is short-lived and highly variable in space and time, so satellite instruments resolve its patterns close to source regions. Across the African continent, mapped temporal correlations between NO2 and CO2 are moderate in magnitude but spatially structured and consistently positive. Although we do not use that association to mechanically convert NO2 observations into CO2, we report it as contextual evidence towards NDCs. Given this context, this study asks the following question: to what extent can socioeconomic development at the neighbourhood scale predict NO2 column densities (the amount of NO2 in the air column above that neighbourhood) across Africa? We apply a convolutional neural network (CNN) to gridded International Wealth Index (IWI) estimates and to NO2 observations from the tropospheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI), and obtain an average predictive accuracy of $$R^2$$ = 0.56 across the African continent. Because IWI can be projected forward, we also present an illustrative 2030 scenario as a methodological demonstration of the relationship between socioeconomic development and NO2 trajectories. These findings indicate that gridded wealth estimates carry predictive information about NO2 column density in Africa. Such estimates offer a lightweight and scalable screening tool that complements process-based atmospheric monitoring rather than replacing it.

business.title: The spillover effects and mechanisms of typhoon disasters on stock volatility: considering the heterogeneity of financial enterprises and non-financial enterprises
business.desc: Extreme meteorological events, such as typhoons, constitute severe external shocks that significantly impact macroeconomic operations and fundamental corporate activities. Grounded in stakeholder theory, this study employs a two way fixed effects difference in differences model alongside the VaR-BEKK-MVGARCH-DUMMY-T framework. Utilizing comprehensive data from the Chinese A share market spanning 2008 to 2024, this study investigates the spillover effects and underlying mechanisms of typhoon disasters on corporate stock volatility. The empirical results demonstrate that typhoon disasters significantly exacerbate the stock volatility of affected enterprises. Furthermore, this study confirms the presence of a unidirectional volatility spillover effect flowing directly from the non-financial sector to the financial sector during these extreme weather events. Subsequent mechanism analysis reveals that typhoons amplify stock price volatility risks across distinct industries through dual pathways. Specifically, these natural disasters diminish the supply chain resilience of non-financial enterprises, while simultaneously destabilizing investor confidence within the financial system by exacerbating widespread uncertainty. This study provides robust micro level evidence for the cross market systemic risk contagion triggered by extreme climate events. It substantially deepens the theoretical understanding of heterogeneous industry risk transmission mechanisms within the growing field of climate finance.

world.title: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
world.desc: Edematous severe childhood malnutrition is distinct from the non-edematous form of malnutrition and remains a major cause of under-five mortality. Its etiology remains unclear, although aberrant one-carbon metabolism has emerged as a potential contributor. Here, we assess genetic variants at loci known to influence one-carbon metabolism, and determine their association with edematous malnutrition in Jamaica and Malawi. Six loci show evidence of association, including four related to homocysteine and folate metabolism - AHCYL1, PRICKLE2, GABBR2, and PLD2, with SNPs at the latter three also having direct effects on homocysteine-related metabolites in Mendelian Randomization. Collectively, one-carbon metabolism-related variants were significantly associated with edematous malnutrition (z = 3.2), with population differences linked to a shared East African genetic ancestry and distinct signatures of selection. These findings strengthen evidence implicating aberrant one-carbon metabolism in edematous malnutrition and highlight the utility of cell-free DNA, intra-continental admixture, and population genetics for mapping disease risk. Edematous malnutrition in children has unclear causes. Here, the authors show that genetic variation at one‑carbon metabolism genes influences disease risk through homocysteine‑related pathways and ancestry‑linked effects in affected populations.

world.title: Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates
world.desc: Conservation areas are critical for tackling the global environmental crisis1. These sites are reported as covering 18.5% of the terrestrial realm2 and governments have committed through Global Biodiversity Framework Target 3 to increase this to at least 30% by 2030 (ref. 3). There are concerns that this potential near-doubling of conservation area coverage will negatively affect vulnerable people and over-stretch conservation resources4. However, nationally available datasets indicate that more conservation areas exist than are reflected in global figures5–7. We evaluated progress towards the area component of Target 3 using a globally representative sample across 25 countries and territories that incorporated these national datasets8. Extrapolating from this sample, we show that conservation areas likely already cover 26.81% of the terrestrial realm. We may be much closer to achieving 30% terrestrial coverage than previously thought. However, we also show that the extra land does not substantially address gaps in ecological representativeness, indicating that solely meeting the area component of Target 3 will do little to solve continuing global biodiversity loss. More focus and resources are needed to achieve the other components of the target, using a more strategic and inclusive approach to fill present gaps and produce equitable and effective conservation area networks. A globally representative sample of 25 countries and territories indicates that conservation areas cover 26.81% of the land, much closer to the 30% by 2030 target than officially reported.
